summary: Tinker Air Force Base is a major United States Air Force installation in Oklahoma City, named after Major General Clarence L. Tinker, the first Native American to reach the rank of major general. It hosts the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex, one of the largest aircraft maintenance and repair facilities in the world, performing depot-level work on B-1B Lancers, B-52 Stratofortresses, E-3 AWACS aircraft, and KC-135 Stratotankers. The base is not a commercial passenger airport; public flight activity is extremely limited and access is restricted to authorized military personnel and contractors.
faqs:
Q: Does Tinker Air Force Base offer commercial passenger flights?
A: No, Tinker is an active military installation and does not provide regular commercial passenger service. Civilian travelers should use Will Rogers World Airport (OKC) in Oklahoma City instead.

Q: What units are stationed at Tinker AFB?
A: The base is home to the Oklahoma City Air Logistics Complex, the 72nd Air Base Wing, Air Force Materiel Command units, and several maintenance and logistics squadrons supporting the Air Force's bomber and tanker fleets.

Q: How large is Tinker Air Force Base?
A: Tinker covers roughly 5,100 acres and employs more than 26,000 military and civilian personnel, making it one of the largest single-site employers in Oklahoma.

Q: Can civilians visit the base?
A: Access is restricted. Visitors without a military ID must be sponsored and pass an installation access check at the gate.
transport_tips: Tinker AFB does not offer scheduled passenger service, so arriving travelers should fly into Will Rogers World Airport (OKC) about 15 miles west of the base. On-base movement is easiest by private vehicle; a military ID or approved visitor pass is required at the gate. Ride-shares and taxis are available at OKC and can drop visitors at the main gate for credential processing.
local_tip: The Tinker Air Force Base Museum is open to the public with base access and features a B-52 bomber, an E-3 AWACS, and other retired aircraft on outdoor display, making it a worthwhile stop for aviation enthusiasts visiting the area.
